statement.p: Three small squares, S_1, S_2, and S_3, each with side 0.01 and centered at the point (1, 1, 3), lie parallel to the xy-, yz- and xz-planes, respectively. The squares are oriented counterclockwise when viewed from the positive z-, x-, and y-axes, respectively. A vector field \vec G has circulation around S_1 of -0.01, around S_2 of -0.0002, and around S_3 of 0.04. Estimate curl \vec G at the point (1, 1, 3)

static.solution:
\vec G has its component in the x-direction given by (\mbox {curl }\vec G)_x \approx \frac{\mbox {Circulation around small square around } x \mbox {-axis}}{\mbox {Area inside square}} = \frac{\mbox {Circulation around }S_2}{\mbox {Area inside }S_2}= \frac{-0.0002}{(0.01)^2} = -2. Similar reasoning leads to (\mbox {curl }\vec G)_y\approx \frac{\mbox {Circulation around } S_3}{\mbox {Area inside }S_3}=\frac{0.04}{(0.01)^2}=400. and (\mbox {curl }\vec G)_z\approx\frac{\mbox {Circulation around } S_1}{\mbox {Area inside }S_1}=\frac{-0.01}{(0.01)^2}=-100.
Thus, \mbox {curl }\vec G\approx -2\,\mathit{\vec i}+400\,\mathit{\vec j}-100\,\mathit{\vec k}.
